question: Should OpenClaw core own this restored recovery-point admission protocol, including its durable journal, hidden CLI controls, and Gateway startup fence, or should core expose a smaller generic seam for host integrations?
rationale: The patch is internally coherent and has direct after-fix evidence, but repository policy reserves lifecycle ownership and fallback behavior for explicit product decisions; source review alone cannot choose the permanent core boundary.

options.title: Defer merge pending RFC boundary acceptance
options.body: Keep the implementation open as evidence while maintainers decide the core-versus-host ownership and the supported upgrade contract.

options.title: Accept the full core protocol
options.body: Merge the journal, private commands, and restored-start fence as OpenClaw’s supported host-neutral recovery contract.

options.title: Reduce to a generic core seam
options.body: Ask for a narrower follow-up that leaves host lifecycle orchestration outside core while preserving only required recovery/readiness primitives.

recommendation.title: Defer merge pending RFC boundary acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep the implementation open as evidence while maintainers decide the core-versus-host ownership and the supported upgrade contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged restart-recovery admission work is the nearest established implementation boundary and provides the most relevant history signal available in this review context.
